--- order: 3 unit: forms title: Join the club introduces: [list-change] recipes: [attribute] summary: "Make the club page's sign-up form work: the form sends its answers, a route reads them, adds the new member and goes back home." language: python hook: "In HTML & CSS the Join button did nothing. Now Python is behind the form, so it can really sign people up." --- In HTML & CSS your club page had a form that went nowhere. With `method="post" action="/join"`, pressing the button **sends** the form's answers to the address `/join`. A route with `methods=["POST"]` receives them, and `request.form["name"]` looks up the box whose `name` attribute is `name`. `members.append(...)` adds the new member to the end of the list. Then `redirect("/")` sends the browser back to the home page. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: club.py#predict check: type: predict q: "You type Zoe and press Join. What does the page show?" options: ["['Ada', 'Zoe']", "['Ada']", "['Zoe']", "An error: Zoe is not in the list"] actual: "['Ada', 'Zoe']. join() appends what was typed in the box named name, then redirect(\"/\") shows the home page again, with the longer list." ``` Follow the answer: the form sends it to `/join`, `join()` appends it, then `redirect("/")` goes back home. ## Run ```step stage: run code: club.py#run try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#run", height: 560 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I signed up two people, then pressed Run again and saw what happened to them." } unlocks: [read-a-form, go-to-another-page] ``` Run it and join the club twice, with different groups. Then press **Run** again: where did the new members go? ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: club.py#run insight: "A form sends each box that has a name attribute; the route reads them with request.form by that name, changes the data, then redirects to a page that shows it." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Why does join() end with redirect(\"/\") instead of returning a page?" options: ["So the browser goes back to the home page, which shows the list with the new member", "To stop the form being sent", "Because POST routes cannot return HTML", "To save the member"] answer: 0 explain: "The home route already shows the members. Redirecting there after a change is the usual pattern, and reloading the page then does not send the form twice." - check: type: question q: "What does request.form[\"group\"] give when someone chooses Champions?" options: ["\"Champions\"", "\"group\"", "The whole form", "3, because it is the third option"] answer: 0 explain: "A select sends the chosen option's text under its name, group." - check: type: bug code: club.py#bug text: "Pressing Join gives 400 Bad Request. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 8 fault: logic misconception: form-name-attr explain: "The box has an id but no name, so the form sends nothing for it, and request.form[\"name\"] has nothing to find. name=\"name\" sends it." ``` ### Back home Why a form ends with a redirect. ### A choice from a list What a select sends. ### Spot the bug A box the form does not send. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "A server must check what it is sent: a blank or wrong answer gets the page back with a message instead of being saved." try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#run", height: 560 } tasks: - hint: - "In join(), after reading name: if name == \"\": return the page with an error message instead of adding the member." - "`render_template_string(PAGE, members=members, error=\"Please type your name.\")`, and in the template `{% if error %}

{{ error }}

{% endif %}`." check: { type: code, text: "If the name is blank, show the page again with a message, and do not add anyone.", rules: { contains: ["if name == \"\""] } } - hint: "Add a Year box with name=\"year\", read it with request.form[\"year\"], store it in the member's dictionary and show it in the list." check: { type: code, text: "Also ask for each member's year level, and show it in the list.", rules: { contains: ["request.form[\"year\"]"] } } ``` ### No blank names Press Join with an empty box: a member with no name appears. Make the app refuse a blank name and say why. ### Year level Ask for each member's **year** as well, and show it in the list. ## Make: record a win ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a form of your own that changes the data, a POST route that reads it, and a redirect to show the change." try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#make", height: 560 } check: { type: code, text: "Add a form to record a win: choose a player, press the button, and their wins go up by 1.", rules: { contains: ["methods=[\"POST\"]", "request.form["] } } ``` Add a form under the results table: a dropdown of the players (made by the template) and an **Add a win** button that adds 1 to that player's wins. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "Why should the server check the name, when the form could just say the box is required?" options: ["Anyone can send anything to /join without using your form, so the server must check what it gets", "Forms cannot check anything", "It is faster", "Browsers ignore required"] answer: 0 explain: "A form's checks help honest users; the server's checks protect the data. Every real web app checks again on the server." ``` The members disappear on every Run, because they live in a variable. Next: save them to a file so they last. ```teacher summary: Students make the club page's sign-up form work with Flask, reading the answers with request.form and redirecting home, then refuse blank names, add a year level and build a form that records a win. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 20 min · Make 10 min goals: - I can send a form to a route with method="post" and read its answers with request.form. - I can explain why a form ends with a redirect. - I can check what a form sends on the server, and reply with a message. before: > Read the unit primer first. `
` sends the form to `/join` when the button is pressed; each box is sent **only if it has a `name` attribute**, under that name (the `id` is for the label; the bug task has an `id` and no `name`, and Flask replies 400 Bad Request). A route accepts a sent form with `methods=["POST"]` and reads it with `request.form["name"]`. After changing the data it returns `redirect("/")`, so the browser shows the home page again (and a reload does not send the form twice). The server checks what it gets (a blank name), because anyone can send anything to an address. Members live in a variable, so they vanish on Run: that motivates the next lesson. In the playground the form is passed to the app by the App tab; on a computer the browser sends it to Flask. running: - "Predict: act it out: one student is the form, one is join(), one is the home page." - "Run: join twice, then press Run. Where did they go?" - "Investigate: in the bug task, ask what the label's for= and the box's id do, and what name= does." - "Modify: test with a blank name and with spaces only (strip() makes them blank)." stuck: - see: 400 Bad Request when the form is sent. ask: Does every box the route reads have a name attribute, spelled the same? fix: name="year" on the box, request.form["year"] in the route. - see: 405 Method Not Allowed. ask: Does the route accept POST? fix: '@app.route("/join", methods=["POST"]).' - see: The error message never shows. ask: Is error passed to the template, and does the template show it? fix: error="..." in render_template_string, and {% if error %}{{ error }}{% endif %} in PAGE. stretch: Refuse a name that is already a member, with its own message. support: Give students the if with the error return, and ask them only to add the error to the template. leads: Next lesson saves the members to a CSV file so they survive a Run. Later, a JSON route lets other programs read the list. exit: q: A form box has id="name" but no name attribute. What does the server get from it? a: "Nothing: only boxes with a name attribute are sent, under that name." explain: > 1. `method="post" action="/join"` sends the form to `/join`; each box with a `name` is sent under that name. 2. The `/join` route reads them with `request.form["name"]` and adds the member. 3. `redirect("/")` sends the browser back home, where the list now has the new member. solutions: step-4#t1: club.py#sol-blank step-4#t2: club.py#sol-year step-5: club.py#sol-make struggle: The name attribute on form boxes. Ask students to list what the form sends, box by box, before they look at the route. ```
